title: Blue Angels Fly High as Ford EV Powers Clean Energy Dream Home at SF Fleet Week
text:
During San Francisco's Fleet Week, the Navy Blue Angels showcased aerial power while a Ford EV-powered home on the Embarcadero highlighted the benefits of transitioning to all-electric living. The display featured modern appliances like induction stoves and zero-emission fireplaces, emphasizing improved indoor air quality and health benefits in light of California's push to phase out gas heaters.
During San Francisco's Fleet Week, as the U.S. Navy Blue Angels flexed their power in the sky, along the Embarcadero a different kind of power popped up and plugged in..
Here, community members and visitors learned and interacted with the electric equipment. The home was powered by a Ford EV.
"While this electric pickup might not be as powerful as a jet plane, it's powerful enough to power the electric dream home for several days," said Kaestner. Inside the structure were modern, clean energy appliances that promise a healthier, more comfortable, and climate-friendly home. It included Kaestner said all-electric homes are a very important step to a carbon-free society.
With California phasing out new natural gas heaters,"So, what you are seeing here is an induction stove that uses magnetism to heat the pot," Kaestner said as he touched a button on the surface to turn it on.. With a gas stove, most of the heat escapes into your kitchen. Induction stoves send energy to the pot bring water to a boil in half the time of what would be needed with a gas stove.
